body:
[A598]

Closes #70

The out-of-context recipe now gives synthesis its clock. `syn/ooc/engine_ooc.tcl` and `syn/ooc/ucpu_ooc.tcl` each read a new constraints file, `syn/ooc/ooc_clock.xdc`, before anything else and therefore before `synth_design`. That file holds the one clock definition, `create_clock -period 10.000 -name clk [get_ports clk_i]`, with the period unchanged at 10 ns. Since the first commit, both scripts issued `create_clock` after `synth_design`; that call is gone. The reported slack is therefore a constrained synthesis result, not a post-hoc report on an unconstrained netlist.

A check, `ooc clock order` (`syn/ooc/check_ooc_clock.py`), holds that the clock was both read in time and in effect, in the `make ooc` flow:

- **Before Vivado starts**, `run.sh` checks both scripts and the XDC.
  - Each script must have exactly one `synth_design` and read `$SPEC/syn/ooc/ooc_clock.xdc` before it. That is this repository's file; a file of the same basename elsewhere does not count.
  - No script may issue `create_clock`, `create_generated_clock`, `read_xdc` or `source` after `synth_design`.
  - The XDC must define exactly one 10.000 ns clock on `clk_i`.
- **After both syntheses**, `run.sh` checks each Vivado log and the timing report beside it, which proves what Vivado actually ran:
  - A `read_xdc` echo of that path must precede `Command: synth_design`.
  - Vivado must report parsing this checkout's `ooc_clock.xdc`, matched by full path, inside synthesis before technology mapping.
  - No constraint command may follow `synth_design completed successfully`.
  - The log must carry no `CRITICAL WARNING`, and its end-of-session count must report 0 critical warnings.
  - The timing report's Clock Summary must be exactly `clk {0.000 5.000} 10.000`.
  - `clk` must be bound to `clk_i`. Each script appends `report_clocks` to its timing report, because the Clock Summary has no source column.
  - `checking no_clock` must report 0.
- **The `ooc` make target runs the check's self-test first.** It has 30 arms: one clean fixture and 29 planted defects. Each arm must be caught by the finding it names, not just by any failure.

No RTL, testbench, bench or repository-script file changes.

## Figures

Re-measured at main `5dce647a` with each flow, using the same setup for both:

- Vivado 2026.1 (lin64, SW Build 6511674) on `xc7a100tfgg484-2`.
- `synth_design -mode out_of_context` with the default directive.
- The shipping ROM and a 10 ns clock on `clk_i`.

The unconstrained column is `make ooc` of main itself. The constrained column is `make ooc` at this head. Its six normalized report bodies are identical to those of the first review head.

| Top | Metric | Unconstrained (create_clock after synth_design) | Constrained (XDC read before synth_design) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| KL_gptp_engine | Slice LUTs | 4,853 | 4,852 |
| KL_gptp_engine | Slice registers | 3,652 | 3,652 |
| KL_gptp_engine | Block RAM tiles | 1.5 | 1.5 |
| KL_gptp_engine | DSPs | 4 | 4 |
| KL_gptp_engine | WNS | +1.773 ns, 0 of 12,254 endpoints failing | +1.773 ns, 0 of 12,254 endpoints failing |
| KL_gptp_ucpu | LUTs / registers / BRAM / DSPs | 1,643 / 733 / 1.5 / 4 | 1,643 / 733 / 1.5 / 4 |
| KL_gptp_ucpu | WNS | +1.941 ns, 0 of 3,165 endpoints failing | +1.941 ns, 0 of 3,165 endpoints failing |

- The only difference is one logic LUT inside the engine's microCPU instance.
- The timing report bodies are identical, with the same critical path and slack.
- The unconstrained run reproduces exactly the dated figures the manager guide carried (PR #76, 2026-09-24), which confirms they came from the unconstrained flow.
- The 2.249 ns cited in the issue is the PR #69-era engine figure; PR #76 later moved it to +1.773 ns.

## Documentation

- `docs/HDL_DEVELOPER.md` gains an "Out-of-context measurement" section. It covers the flow, what the check holds before and after synthesis, both flows side by side with a Flow column and the tool identity, and a checklist item.
- `docs/MANAGER.md` gives each figure in the latest snapshot its flow. It keeps the PR #76 delta and labels it as the unconstrained flow.
- Every archived page that quotes out-of-context figures gains a flow note under its banner; no archived figure changes.
  - For this line's pages, the note records that `syn/ooc` issued `create_clock` after `synth_design` from the first commit `c99f7a8` through `5dce647a`.
  - For the prototype pages, the order is verified at `c99f7a8` only, because the prototype line's later scripts are not retained.

## Validation

At this head, with Verilator 5.050 first on the path, each command ran from the repository root:

| Command | Exit | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| `make tb` | 0 | microCPU 768/768; parser 268/268; engine 1,613/1,613 in the shipping, request-seeded and Sync-seeded images; engine mutation arm 34/34; gaskets 81/81 plus 5/5 controls; tsn-gen 288/288 plus 4/4 controls; bench tag test PASS; no skips (fresh build) |
| `make contract` | 0 | PHC interface contract PASS |
| `make lint` | 0 | engine and bench lint clean |
| `make docs` | 0 | diagram check and self-test PASS; docs check PASS (11 current, 17 historical pages) and self-test PASS; source evidence 20 exact, 0 findings, self-test PASS |
| `make ooc` | 0 | `ooc clock order` self-test PASS (30 arms); script check PASS; both syntheses 0 critical warnings and 0 errors; post-synthesis check PASS on both logs and timing reports; six reports retained; tree clean afterwards |

Both logs show the clock defined before synthesis. Both timing reports show it in effect on `clk_i`:

```text
ucpu_ooc.log    28:# read_xdc $SPEC/syn/ooc/ooc_clock.xdc   32:Command: synth_design ...   84:Parsing XDC File [.../syn/ooc/ooc_clock.xdc]   372:Start Technology Mapping   486:... 0 Critical Warnings ...
engine_ooc.log  28:# read_xdc $SPEC/syn/ooc/ooc_clock.xdc   38:Command: synth_design ...   116:Parsing XDC File [.../syn/ooc/ooc_clock.xdc]  443:Start Technology Mapping   565:... 0 Critical Warnings ...
*_timing.rpt    1. checking no_clock (0)   clk    {0.000 5.000}      10.000          100.000   clk    10.000      {0.000 5.000}  P           {clk_i}
```

Planted controls on real synthesis. Each was one Vivado at a time, in scratch copies; no RTL in this tree changed.

- **Clock port renamed in the microCPU** (the first review's arm). The script check passes, and Vivado completes with two `create_clock:No valid object(s) found` critical warnings. The post-synthesis check fails with six findings:
  - both critical-warning lines;
  - `session ends with 2 critical warnings`;
  - `Clock Summary is []`;
  - `clock clk is not bound to clk_i`;
  - `checking no_clock reports ['1003']`.
- **Engine top's clock port renamed**, run through `run.sh`. The microCPU passes, and the engine fails with the same six kinds of finding (`no_clock` 4412). `run.sh` exits 1.
- **8 ns clock, script check bypassed.** The post check fails with `Clock Summary is ['clk {0.000 4.000} 8.000 125.000']`. The script check alone names the 8 ns XDC.
- **A byte-identical `ooc_clock.xdc` read from another directory, script check bypassed.** The post check fails with `... is not read before synth_design` and `synth_design did not parse <this checkout's ooc_clock.xdc> before mapping`.
- **Unplanted head:** PASS.

Planted controls on the script check, run through `make ooc` with a stub in place of the synthesis tool. Each of these stops the run before synthesis, by name:

- Moving `read_xdc` after `synth_design`, in either script.
- `read_xdc /nonexistent/ooc_clock.xdc`.
- A second `create_clock` in the XDC.
- An 8 ns XDC.
- Restoring main's scripts.

The unplanted control reaches the stub.

Self-test mutation sweep: each rule of the check was disabled, or narrowed to a basename or a first row, in turn. All 24 of 24 mutants fail the self-test, each on the arm it should.

## Round 2

Changes since the first review head `26622e27`:

- The post-synthesis check now fails unless the clock took effect. The review's renamed-port synthesis, which passed before, now fails by name.
  - The new rules: no critical warning, an end-of-session critical-warning count of 0, Clock Summary `clk` at 10 ns, `clk` bound to `clk_i` (`report_clocks` appended to each timing report) and `no_clock` 0.
  - The XDC is matched by full path in the scripts and in the logs.
  - New self-test arms: the renamed port, a foreign `ooc_clock.xdc` of the same basename, a wrong period, a critical-warning count above zero, an XDC with two `create_clock` lines, and one arm for each remaining new branch.
  - The `run.sh` header and the check's docstring now state exactly what is held.
- `docs/HDL_DEVELOPER.md` describes the post-synthesis rules. The pre-#70 note now reads "This repository's `syn/ooc` figures before #70 were unconstrained."

## Known limitations

- Out-of-context synthesis is not board timing qualification; no placement or routing was run.
- The microCPU source carries a comment quoting the other repository's 1,070-LUT anchor. This change leaves RTL untouched. The flow behind that anchor is described in the `ucpu_ooc.tcl` header instead.
- Comparing against figures dated before this change needs a run in the old order. The guides label every quoted figure with its flow for that reason.
- The script check requires the literal `$SPEC/syn/ooc/ooc_clock.xdc` argument, but it does not evaluate `SPEC`. A redirected `SPEC` is caught after synthesis, by the full-path parse rule.
title: Constrain the OOC clock before synthesis and record both flows' figures (#70)
